newsitem.title: USA: Roanoke Electric sees improved margins.
newsitem.headline: Roanoke Electric sees improved margins.

text.p: Roanoke Electric Steel Corp said on Friday that it expects improved first quarter margins because of falling steel scrap prices.

"With no signs of recession and with markets continuing to look favorable, the prospects are encouraging for another good year in fiscal 1997," Roanoke Electric said. The company's fiscal year ends October 1997.
Roanoke, a mini-mill producer of finished steel, processes steel scrap through one of its subsidiaries, the company said.
Backlogs that the beginning of the fiscal year and selling values of fabricated products are "excellent," while backlogs for mill products are "at comfortable levels," Roanoke said.
Selling prices for mill products, however, continue to be depressed, Roanoke said.
In the year ended October 1996, Roanoke Electric said gross profit margins narrowed during the year because of lower prices for mill products.
Strong business conditions continued in the construction industry, helping margins for fabricated products, Roanoke Electric said.
Billet shipments and earnings were hurt by a planned shutdown of its melt shop to intall a new furnace and upgrade an electric arc furnace, Roanoke Electric said.
